newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow to use all means to save Tajik hostages.
newsitem.headline: Moscow to use all means to save Tajik hostages.

text.p: Russia is ready to use all means necessary to save the lives of Russian and Western hostages held in Tajikistan, Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday, according to Itar-Tass news agency.

"The leadership of all Russian military services and the Foreign Ministry...will do all possible on their part," Chernomyrdin told reporters after talking by telephone with Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov late on Thursday.
"We have warned our armed forces and we ask the government of Rakhmonov to take all necessary measures."

Chernomyrdin spoke with the Tajik president after reports from Russian journalists held captive by Islamic fighters Bakhram and Rizvon Sadirov said a United Nations military observer held hostage had been shot dead.
He said neither Russia nor Tajikistan could confirm the reports, but expressed hope that all of the more than a dozen hostages would be released on Friday, Tass said.
President Boris Yeltsin, who is maintaining a limited work schedule as he recovers from pneumonia, is following the situation, Chernomyrdin said.

On Friday, Russian officials would also consider sending Defence Minister Igor Rodionov to Tajikistan, Chernomyrdin said. He also said the Tajik leader Rakhmonov told him he planned to travel to the region where the hostages were held.
As he raised the spectre of a more active Russian response to the situation, Chernomyrdin said the Tajik president was ready to meet the rebels' demands.
"Imomali Rakhmonov told me he plans to travel to the place of these events. He also gave the order to fulfill all of Sadirov's demands," Chernomyrdin was quoted as saying.
The Tajik rebel leader is demanding 40 rebels as well as arms and military supplies before he releases the hostages, Chernomyrdin said.

The hostages were expected to be released on Thursday after the Tajik government said it had flown in 40 rebels from neighbouring Afghanistan to swap for the hostages. But talks broke down over the details, a spokesman for the Tajik president said.
